__**Disclaimer : This guide is susceptible of changes due to patch notes reworks of interactions.**__

Traphase is a online RNG PVP turn based gamemode with a MTG like gameplay style.

__**General Tips**__

In Traphase there are 5 types of classes, Guardian ( Blue ), Warborn ( Red ), Luminis ( Purple ), Malphas ( Yellow ), Divinia ( Green ).
But for simplicity we will refer them by their colors.

- NEVER THINK OF EACH CLASSES AS A DEFINITE TYPE OF CLASS, for example Blue type units who are supposed to be tank can also become DPS depending on the wheel equipped on, Green type units who are supposed to be healer can also become DPS, Red type units can sometimes also become healers and so does yellow.

They can be close to some kind of classes but not define into them.

- READ THE KITS OF THE UNITS!!!

- At low elo on both gamemode you won't lose many points if you lose the matches and you will most likely face against bots so it's better to enjoy limit testing there until you're ready to try and climb ( beginner protection up to 1500 elo ).

- Precise Match button = the matchmaking will take longer but you won't have to deal with matchmakings like 5k elo vs 100 elo. It's more targeted to your elo range.

- Simulated Rival button = you will be more likely to face against bots and after 180 sec of matchmaking it will be a forced match against a bot.

- Each units have the same HP pool and damages as the opposing side and is not affected by dupes ( for example Leigh have base 70 max HP, if your opponent have a +12 leigh in their rooster, their leigh will still remain at 70 max HP ).

- The Position of each units during team building : the most far left unit will be on the rear meanwhile the most far right will be in front, it's up to you to place your units depending on your needs.

- Each start of turns let you draw 6 cards and your max hand size is 10 so it's generally more ideal to have a low card count ( 4 or under ) in your hand at the end of the turn to draw as much as possible, although you can also stash your cards depending on if you want to counter play your opponent's next move in the next turn.

- You start at 3 arithmetica, each start of turns gives you +1 arithmetica max and goes up to 10 arithmetica max.

- Each end of turns gives you 10 alienus.

- The player who start 2nd gets a card that let them draw 3 cards + get 3 arithmetica.

- Some debuff effects have also additional gimmicks such as :
 Void removing all delayed Alienus gain on the target,
 Blighten removing all delayed heal + shield,
 Paralysis not only double the damages dealt in the same turn by another Paralysis damage but also double any stacks that comes with it ( for example if a card have deal 8 paralysis damages + poison, if the target already got paralyzed then it will becomes 16 stacks of poison ),
 Enhance buff remove weakness debuff.

- Invincibility state from Arachne can be bypassed by Sacrifice or Poison trigger skill card.

- There is something called mulligan, when you start the battle against your opponent, you have a phase to choose what cards you want to be reshuffled from your first hand.

That phase compose of 5 selectable cards to be discarded, you can choose none too, discarded cards through that method will force them into an RNG draw ( previous patches made them last draw of your deck ).

__**All Pick**__

In All pick gamemode you need to own the unit / wheel / posse to be able to use them, it's a bit hard to enjoy that gamemode especially against meta teams when you don't own certain specific wheels or units to enable an entire team so i would recommend you to at least try to get a decent amount of both before trying that gamemode.

Some wheels are also locked behind BP and others specific SSR wheels doesn't have any rerun so far so it's quite hard for F2P to play on this gamemode early on.

Although you can unlock everything TEMPORARILY by buying the premium version of the BP.

__**Draft Pick**__

In Draft Pick gamemode you don't need to own anything in order to properly enjoy the gamemode, however, it is incredibly more RNG compared to the original counterpart so beware.

You will be given 4 type of classes between the 5 said previously, each have 3 units per classes, also a set of wheels and posses you can choose from.

Only one unit class can be chosen during the picking phase so if your opponent chooses for example 1 unit from blue then you don't have to decide between who you choose from there so you can counterpick them with another pick during early pick.

This advice won't be 100% foolproof on that gamemode due to high amount of RNG but it will gives you a closer winning chances.

1) Check relic,
2) Check units,
3) Check WoD,
4) See if there is some combo between units + WoD or units + units
5) Sometimes the combo can get bricked by the relic,
6) Posse are situational, but some are extremely good to have stuff like stagnation 3 pierce or void,
7) Aim for counterpick, If the enemy take strike based unit then you take para posse stuff or like that,
8) Based on the relic you change your playstyle, for example you got the relic that reshuffle your hand every turns, you discards all of your high cost wheel if you have more than 2 or 3 in starting hand.

- You can also change the position of your units at the end of the picking phase before completely locking in.
Thanks for the guide; will you make a google doc?
